concepts.name: Weather elements, instruments and the weather station
concepts.description: Weather versus climate; the elements of weather (temperature, rainfall, humidity, pressure, wind speed and direction, sunshine, cloud cover); the instruments that measure them (thermometers including maximum-minimum and wet-and-dry bulb, rain gauge, barometer, wind vane, anemometer, sunshine recorder) and how to read and record them; siting a weather station and the Stevenson screen. Out: synoptic charts and forecasting (geo.weather.synoptic-forecasting).

concepts.name: Synoptic charts and weather forecasting
concepts.description: Synoptic (weather map) symbols for cloud cover, wind, precipitation and fronts; isobars and pressure systems on a weather map; reading a simple synoptic chart; what forecasting is, why it matters (farming, aviation, disaster warnings) and indigenous knowledge indicators used to forecast rain in Zimbabwe. Out: drawing climate graphs (geo.weather.climate-graphs).

concepts.name: Weather and climate data: tables, statistics and climate graphs
concepts.description: Recording weather data in tables; calculating mean daily and monthly temperature, temperature range, annual range and total rainfall; drawing and interpreting climate graphs (temperature line over rainfall bars) and describing a climate from one. Out: general statistics and other graph types (geo.skills.data-analysis, geo.skills.graphs).

concepts.name: Precipitation and the types of rainfall
concepts.description: Forms of precipitation (rain, drizzle, hail, snow, dew, frost); how rain forms (evaporation, rising air, adiabatic cooling, dew point, condensation, cloud droplets growing); convectional, relief (orographic, including rain shadow) and frontal rainfall with annotated diagrams; where each type occurs in Zimbabwe and the world.

concepts.name: Weather hazards: floods, lightning and drought
concepts.description: Weather hazards that affect Zimbabwe and southern Africa (floods, lightning, drought, hailstorms, heatwaves, frost): their causes, impacts on people and the economy, and measures to reduce them; how human activities change local weather. Out: tropical cyclones (geo.weather.tropical-cyclones) and river-flood management (geo.rivers.flooding).

concepts.name: The climate of Zimbabwe and climate variability
concepts.description: Zimbabwe's seasons (hot wet, cool dry, hot dry), the influence of latitude, altitude and distance from the sea, temperature and rainfall patterns across the country and its climatic zones; how climate relates to farming, tourism and other activities; climate variability (rainfall and temperature anomalies, mid-season dry spells, El Niño-related droughts) and responses. Out: the natural farming regions (geo.agriculture.natural-regions).

concepts.name: Air masses and the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone
concepts.description: What an air mass is, how air masses are classified (tropical/polar, maritime/continental) and their characteristics; the air streams affecting Zimbabwe and southern Africa (south-east trades, north-east monsoon, north-west airflow from the Congo basin); the ITCZ, its seasonal shift between January and July and the weather it brings.

concepts.name: World climate types
concepts.description: The basis of global climate classification; the main climate types and their temperature and rainfall characteristics: tropical (equatorial, tropical continental/savanna, tropical desert, tropical monsoon), warm temperate (Mediterranean, warm temperate east coast) and cool temperate and polar climates; their world and African distribution.

concepts.name: Temperate depressions and fronts
concepts.description: How mid-latitude (temperate) depressions form along the polar front, their structure (warm and cold sectors, warm, cold and occluded fronts) and the sequence of weather as a depression passes; anticyclones in contrast; where depressions occur.

concepts.name: Tropical cyclones (hurricanes and typhoons)
concepts.description: Global distribution and seasons of tropical cyclones; conditions for and stages of formation; structure (eye, eye wall); hazards (strong winds, storm surges, flooding, landslides); impacts and the four Ps of management (prediction, preparation, planning, protection); a named cyclone case study such as Cyclone Idai (2019) in Mozambique and eastern Zimbabwe.

concepts.name: Climate change: evidence and causes
concepts.description: Evidence of climate change (temperature records, ice cores, sea-ice extent, glacier retreat, historical records); natural causes (Milankovitch orbital cycles, sunspots, volcanic eruptions); the natural and enhanced greenhouse effect and human causes (burning fossil fuels, deforestation, agriculture, cement); local human influence on weather and climate (urban heat islands, dams and lakes, deforestation, desertification).

concepts.name: Impacts of climate change
concepts.description: Present and predicted impacts at global, regional and national scales: rising temperatures and sea levels, changing rainfall patterns, more extreme events, effects on food production, water supply, ecosystems, health and the economy; impacts on Zimbabwe and southern Africa (droughts, heat, shifting farming regions); positive and negative impacts. Out: farming adaptation in detail (geo.agriculture.climate-pests).

concepts.name: Responding to climate change: mitigation and adaptation
concepts.description: Mitigation (renewable energy, efficiency, afforestation, carbon capture, transport) and adaptation (water storage, drought-tolerant crops, flood defences, early warning); international agreements (UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol, Paris Agreement) and national strategies; evaluating them; a named country or region example of impacts and responses.

concepts.name: Major landforms and the relief of Zimbabwe
concepts.description: Landforms versus landscape; major landforms (mountains, plateaus, plains, escarpments, valleys, hills, inselbergs) in the local area, Zimbabwe, Africa and the world; Zimbabwe's relief regions (Highveld, Middleveld, Lowveld, Eastern Highlands, Zambezi and Save-Limpopo lowlands) and the benefits of landforms to people.

concepts.name: Rocks: igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic
concepts.description: How the three rock groups form, their characteristics and examples (granite, basalt, dolerite; sandstone, shale, limestone, coal; gneiss, marble, quartzite, slate); the rock cycle in outline; rocks of Zimbabwe (granite country, the Great Dyke, Karoo sediments and basalts) and their uses.

concepts.name: Weathering, mass wasting and the landforms they produce
concepts.description: Physical (exfoliation, block and granular disintegration, frost action) and chemical (hydrolysis, oxidation, carbonation, solution) weathering and the factors controlling them; granite landforms (kopjes/tors, castle kopjes, dwalas/bornhardts, balancing rocks) and karst features (caves, sinkholes, stalactites, stalagmites); mass wasting (soil creep, landslides, mudflows, rockfalls), its hazards and disaster risk management.

concepts.name: Arid and semi-arid regions and wind action
concepts.description: Characteristics and distribution of arid and semi-arid regions in Zimbabwe, Africa and the world and the factors that cause them; wind erosion (deflation, abrasion), transport (suspension, saltation, surface creep) and deposition; landforms such as sand dunes (barchans, seif dunes), rock pedestals, zeugen, yardangs, mesas, buttes, inselbergs and pediments; the role of water in deserts.

concepts.name: The Earth's structure, continental drift and moving plates
concepts.description: Layers of the Earth (inner core, outer core, mantle, crust, lithosphere, asthenosphere) and their characteristics; continental drift theory and its evidence; plate tectonics: the main plates and how they move (convection currents, ridge push, slab pull). Out: boundary types and processes (geo.tectonics.plate-boundaries).

concepts.name: Plate boundaries and the distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes
concepts.description: Divergent (constructive), convergent (destructive and collision) and conservative (transform) boundaries; the processes and landforms at each (ridges, rift valleys, trenches, fold mountains, volcanic island arcs); why earthquakes and volcanoes occur where they do; hot spots; implications of plate movement for climate over geological time.

concepts.name: Folding and faulting and the resulting landforms
concepts.description: Compression and tension; types of folds (simple, asymmetrical, overfold, recumbent) and fold mountains; types of faults (normal, reverse, tear) and resulting landforms (rift valleys, block mountains/horsts, escarpments, fault-line valleys); examples including the East African Rift Valley and faulted valleys in Zimbabwe such as the mid-Zambezi valley.

concepts.name: Volcanoes: types, features and hazards
concepts.description: Causes of volcanic activity; types of volcano (strato-volcano/composite cone, shield, cinder cone) and their features (crater, vent, magma chamber, secondary cone); active, dormant and extinct volcanoes; volcanic hazards (lava flows, ash fall, pyroclastic flows, lahars, tephra, gases) and the significance of speed, size, frequency and spread; intrusive landforms (dykes, sills, batholiths) in outline; benefits of volcanoes.

concepts.name: Earthquakes: causes, characteristics and measurement
concepts.description: Causes of earthquakes; focus, epicentre and seismic waves; measuring magnitude and intensity (moment magnitude, Richter and Mercalli scales; the volcanic explosivity index for eruptions); secondary effects (tsunamis, liquefaction, landslides, fires); earthquakes in southern Africa.

concepts.name: Living with tectonic hazards: why people stay and the impacts
concepts.description: Why people live in areas at risk from earthquakes and volcanoes (fertile soils, geothermal energy, minerals, tourism, jobs, attachment to place, poverty, confidence in protection); social, economic and environmental impacts of earthquakes and eruptions, short and long term; factors that make some events more damaging than others (magnitude, depth, population density, building quality, level of development, time of day).

concepts.name: Managing tectonic hazards
concepts.description: Primary and secondary responses; monitoring and prediction (seismometers, tiltmeters, gas sampling, satellites), protection (earthquake-resistant buildings and retrofitting), planning (hazard mapping, land-use zoning, drills, emergency kits) and technology; disaster risk management; evaluating these strategies; named earthquake and volcanic eruption case studies with causes, impacts and responses.

concepts.name: Drainage basins, the water cycle and river regimes
concepts.description: The drainage basin as part of the water cycle: inputs, stores, flows and outputs (precipitation, interception, infiltration, percolation, overland flow, throughflow, groundwater flow, channel flow, evaporation, transpiration); basin features (source, mouth, watershed, tributary, confluence); river channel characteristics and the Bradshaw model; seasonal river regimes in Zimbabwe and the Zambezi, Save and Limpopo basins; simple flood hydrographs.

concepts.name: River processes: erosion, transportation and deposition
concepts.description: Erosion (hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition, solution) vertical and lateral; transportation (traction, saltation, suspension, solution); why and where deposition happens; how energy, velocity and discharge change downstream. Out: the landforms produced (geo.rivers.landforms-upper, geo.rivers.landforms-lower).

concepts.name: River landforms of erosion: waterfalls, gorges and V-shaped valleys
concepts.description: Characteristics and formation of V-shaped valleys, interlocking spurs, potholes, rapids, waterfalls and gorges, with annotated sequences of diagrams described in words; the Victoria Falls and Batoka Gorge as a named example.

concepts.name: River landforms of deposition: meanders, floodplains and deltas
concepts.description: Characteristics and formation of meanders (river cliffs, slip-off slopes), oxbow lakes, floodplains, levées, braiding and deltas (arcuate, bird's-foot, estuarine) with diagrams described in words; named examples.

concepts.name: River opportunities, flood hazards and flood management
concepts.description: Opportunities of living near rivers (water, fertile soil, transport, HEP, fishing, tourism) and hazards; natural and human causes of floods; impacts; hard and soft management (dams, levées, channelisation, afforestation, floodplain zoning, warning systems); evaluation including sustainability; a named flood case study (for example floods in the Muzarabani area of the lower Zambezi valley or below the Tokwe-Mukosi dam in 2014).

concepts.name: River pollution and its management
concepts.description: Human causes of river pollution (sewage, industrial effluent, mining, agricultural run-off, solid waste), impacts on people and ecosystems (eutrophication, water-borne disease), management strategies and techniques and their evaluation; a named polluted river case study.

concepts.name: Coastal processes: waves, erosion, transport and deposition
concepts.description: Constructive and destructive waves and wave refraction; marine erosion (hydraulic action, corrasion/abrasion, corrosion/solution, attrition); transportation and longshore drift; why deposition happens; sub-aerial processes on cliffs in outline. Out: the landforms produced (geo.coasts.landforms).

concepts.name: Coastal landforms and coastline types
concepts.description: Characteristics and formation of erosional landforms (headlands and bays, cliffs, wave-cut platforms, caves, arches, stacks, stumps) and depositional landforms (beaches, spits, bars, sand dunes), with diagrams described in words; concordant and discordant coastlines.

concepts.name: Coastal opportunities, hazards and management
concepts.description: Opportunities and hazards of living on the coast; causes and impacts of coastal erosion and flooding; hard engineering (sea walls, groynes, rock armour, gabions) and soft engineering (beach nourishment, dune regeneration, managed retreat) evaluated, including sustainability; a named coastline case study of erosion and its management.

concepts.name: Coral reefs and mangroves
concepts.description: Global distribution and the conditions coral reefs and mangroves need; their importance (biodiversity, coastal protection, fisheries, tourism); threats (warming and bleaching, pollution, overfishing, clearance for development); strategies to protect and manage them; a named coral reef case study.

concepts.name: Ecosystems: components, food chains and food webs
concepts.description: Systems and ecosystems; biotic and abiotic components; inputs, processes and outputs; micro-ecosystems such as a pond, termite mound or vlei; producers, consumers and decomposers; food chains, food webs and pyramids of numbers and energy; interdependence. Out: nutrient cycles (geo.ecosystems.nutrient-cycles).

concepts.name: Nutrient, nitrogen and carbon cycles
concepts.description: The nutrient cycle (stores in biomass, litter and soil and the transfers between them), the nitrogen cycle and the carbon cycle in outline; how cycles differ between ecosystems and how human activity disrupts them; why the cycles matter.

concepts.name: Biodiversity and the value of ecosystems
concepts.description: Species, habitat and genetic diversity; habitats in a local ecosystem; benefits of ecosystems (timber, fuel, fruits, honey, medicines, oxygen, carbon sinks, soil protection, rainfall); using ecosystems sustainably for small businesses such as eco-tourism, beekeeping and crafts. Out: conservation methods (geo.ecosystems.conservation-restoration).

concepts.name: Conserving and restoring ecosystems
concepts.description: Threats to local ecosystems (veld fires, deforestation, overgrazing, soil erosion); conservation measures (fireguards, tree planting, terracing, alternative energy such as biogas and solar, destocking, legislation, indigenous knowledge systems) and restoration (gully reclamation, grass and tree planting); the meaning of sustainable ecosystem management.

concepts.name: Wetlands
concepts.description: Types of wetland (vleis/dambos, marshes, swamps, floodplains); their importance and benefits (water storage and purification, flood control, grazing, biodiversity, crafts); threats (drainage, cultivation, building, pollution) and protection (the Ramsar Convention, environmental law); wetlands in Zimbabwe.

concepts.name: The tropical rainforest ecosystem
concepts.description: Global distribution; the equatorial climate (overhead sun, low pressure, convectional rain, high temperatures); layered structure (emergents, canopy, under-canopy, shrub layer, forest floor); soils and rapid nutrient cycling; interrelationships between climate, soil, plants, animals and people; adaptations of plants and animals.

concepts.name: Threats to tropical rainforests and their management
concepts.description: Causes of deforestation (logging, farming, cattle ranching, mining, roads, HEP, settlement); local and global impacts; management strategies and techniques (protected areas, selective logging, agroforestry, ecotourism, debt-for-nature swaps, international agreements) evaluated; a named rainforest case study.

concepts.name: Savanna and hot desert biomes
concepts.description: Location, climate, vegetation, soils and plant and animal adaptations of the tropical continental (savanna) biome, including the miombo and mopane woodlands of Zimbabwe, and of the tropical (hot) desert biome; inputs, processes and outputs of each; the role of fire and grazing in savannas.

concepts.name: The Antarctic ecosystem
concepts.description: Location of Antarctica; its climate (high pressure, high latitude, low sun angle, very low temperatures and precipitation); features of the ecosystem (ice sheet, sea ice, marine food web based on krill); interrelationships between abiotic and biotic factors; adaptations of plants and animals.

concepts.name: Threats to Antarctica and its management
concepts.description: Threats (climate change, fishing, resource exploitation, tourism, pollution); impacts of damage to the ecosystem; management through international agreements (the Antarctic Treaty and its environmental protocol, fishing conservation agreements), environmental impact assessment and tourism guidelines, evaluated.

concepts.name: Soils: components, properties, formation and profiles
concepts.description: Soil components (minerals, organic matter, water, air); properties (texture, structure, colour, pH, organic and mineral content); sand, clay and loam; soil-forming factors and processes in the tropics (including leaching, laterisation, gleying and cheluviation) and the soils they form; soil profiles and horizons; simple soil tests.

concepts.name: Natural resources: types, population pressure and exploitation
concepts.description: What natural resources are; renewable and non-renewable resources; sustainable use in the local area; the relationship between population growth and resources (pressure, over- and under-population in outline); factors influencing the exploitation of resources in Zimbabwe and Africa.

concepts.name: Conserving water, forests and fish
concepts.description: Why resources need conserving; methods of conserving water (dams, harvesting, recycling, efficient irrigation), forests (afforestation, controlled cutting, alternative fuels), fish (quotas, closed seasons, net sizes, fish farming) and soil (in outline); examples from Zimbabwe such as Lake Kariba fisheries and Forestry Commission plantations.

concepts.name: Wildlife management, human-wildlife conflict and CAMPFIRE
concepts.description: Types of protected area (national parks, safari areas, sanctuaries, conservancies, game parks) and examples in Zimbabwe (Hwange, Gonarezhou, Mana Pools, Matobo); benefits and problems of wildlife management; problem versus dangerous animals; causes of and solutions to human-wildlife conflict; the CAMPFIRE programme: reasons, benefits and sustainability, with a named district case study.

concepts.name: Types of energy: renewable and non-renewable
concepts.description: Renewable (solar, wind, HEP, biomass and biogas, geothermal, tidal, wave), non-renewable (coal, oil, natural gas, nuclear) and fuelwood (renewable or not depending on use); uses of energy; the economic importance of energy to agriculture, mining and manufacturing; the advantages and disadvantages of each source, including environmental impacts and costs.

concepts.name: Generating electricity and siting power stations
concepts.description: How electricity is generated in HEP, thermal (coal, gas, geothermal), nuclear, solar and wind plants; factors influencing the siting of power stations; Zimbabwe's main stations (Kariba South HEP and Hwange thermal) and the Kariba scheme; environmental impacts of generation and mitigation (reforestation, cleaner energy).

concepts.name: Global energy supply, demand and energy security
concepts.description: Reasons for rising global production and consumption of energy; global patterns of energy surplus and deficit; energy security and why it matters; reasons for differences in energy use within and between countries at different levels of development.

concepts.name: Managing energy supplies sustainably
concepts.description: Strategies and techniques to increase energy supply (new reserves, renewables, imports, interconnectors) and to conserve energy (efficiency, public transport, energy-saving technologies such as biogas digesters and efficient stoves); evaluation including sustainability; energy policies; a named country case study of its energy mix and management, for example Zimbabwe.

concepts.name: Maps: components, types and symbols
concepts.description: Components of a good map (title, frame, grid, key/legend, scale, north point, source); topographical, political, physical and economic maps; conventional (universal) symbols on topographical maps; sketch maps of the local area. Out: thematic statistical maps (geo.maps.thematic-maps).

concepts.name: Thematic maps: choropleth, isoline, flow-line and others
concepts.description: Constructing and interpreting thematic maps: choropleth, isoline, dot distribution, proportional symbols, flow-line and desire-line maps, sphere-of-influence and route maps; choosing a suitable map; strengths and limitations.

concepts.name: Location: grid references, latitude, longitude and time zones
concepts.description: Eastings and northings; four- and six-figure grid references and locating features; latitude and longitude in degrees and minutes; the UTM grid in outline; time zones and calculating local time from longitude (15 degrees per hour), the Prime Meridian and the International Date Line.

concepts.name: Scale, distance and area
concepts.description: Statement, representative-fraction and linear scales and converting between them; measuring straight-line and curved (winding) distances on maps (string, paper edge, dividers); using Pythagoras' theorem for distances; estimating area by counting grid squares and with graph paper.

concepts.name: Direction and bearings
concepts.description: Compass points (8 and 16 point); true, grid and magnetic north; bearings measured clockwise from grid north with a protractor; back bearings; navigating with a magnetic compass.

concepts.name: Relief on maps: contours and landforms
concepts.description: Contour lines, contour interval, spot heights and trigonometrical stations; working out altitude; recognising landforms from contour patterns (hills, ridges, spurs, valleys, cols, plateaus, escarpments, conical hills) and slope types (gentle, steep, concave, convex, uniform); describing relief and drainage from a map.

concepts.name: Gradient, cross-sections and intervisibility
concepts.description: Calculating gradient as vertical interval over horizontal equivalent (1 in n, percentage); interpreting gradient for roads, railways and farming; drawing and interpreting cross-sections and transects (with vertical exaggeration); intervisibility between two points.

concepts.name: Interpreting human and physical patterns on maps
concepts.description: Identifying land use on topographical maps and the factors behind it; settlement patterns and functions; drainage patterns (dendritic, trellis, radial, parallel); transport networks and their relationship to relief; point, line and area (polygon) data.

concepts.name: Photographs, satellite images and remote sensing
concepts.description: Ground, oblique and vertical aerial photographs; interpreting photographs and satellite images (foreground, middle ground, background; features and land use); remote sensing; light as a wave and the electromagnetic spectrum (visible bands, near-infrared, false-colour images) applied to image interpretation; annotating and evaluating images.

concepts.name: GPS and GIS: layers, Boolean logic and overlay analysis
concepts.description: How the Global Positioning System works and navigating with GPS; what a geographical information system is (data layers, attributes, point, line and polygon data); Boolean logic (intersection AND, union OR, complement NOT) shown with Venn diagrams; overlay analysis using relational and conditional statements to solve simple spatial problems (for example siting a facility); benefits and limitations of GIS.

concepts.name: Graphs, charts and diagrams
concepts.description: Choosing, constructing and interpreting bar graphs (simple, compound and divided), line graphs, pie charts, pictograms, histograms, scatter graphs with lines of best fit, triangular graphs, radial graphs, rose charts, kite graphs, dispersion graphs, population pyramids (construction only; see geo.population.structure), proportional symbols, flow diagrams and systems diagrams; describing trends and patterns from them. Out: climate graphs (geo.weather.climate-graphs) and thematic maps (geo.maps.thematic-maps).

concepts.name: Statistics and data analysis in geography
concepts.description: Mean, median, mode, range and interquartile range; percentages, ratios, proportions and rates; significant figures and standard notation; describing relationships between data sets; interpolation and extrapolation; identifying anomalies and limitations of data; drawing conclusions from statistics.

concepts.name: The route to geographical enquiry
concepts.description: The stages of an investigation: identifying a question, aims and hypotheses; deciding what data to collect and how; collecting, selecting and presenting data; analysis and interpretation; conclusions about the hypothesis; evaluating methods, accuracy and reliability and suggesting further work; risk assessment and working safely.

concepts.name: Human fieldwork: sampling, questionnaires, counts and surveys
concepts.description: Sampling (random, systematic, stratified, opportunistic; sample size; pilot surveys); designing and conducting questionnaires and interviews; pedestrian and traffic counts and recording sheets; environmental quality and bi-polar surveys; land-use surveys and delimiting a CBD or sphere of influence; collecting population data in a school or community.

concepts.name: Physical fieldwork: rivers, beaches, vegetation and weather
concepts.description: Equipment and techniques for physical investigations: river width, depth, velocity (flow meter or float), cross-sectional area and discharge; bedload size and roundness; beach profiles with ranging poles and clinometer; pebble size and longshore drift; quadrats and transects for vegetation; microclimate measurements; recording sheets and accuracy.

concepts.name: Zimbabwe's minerals: geology, distribution and importance
concepts.description: Minerals and ores; mineral groups (metallic: precious, ferrous, base; non-metallic; energy minerals); Zimbabwe's geological formations (greenstone gold belts, the Great Dyke, Karoo coal basins) and the distribution of its main minerals and mines (gold, platinum, chrome, nickel, coal, diamonds, lithium, iron ore, copper, asbestos); the economic importance of minerals to Zimbabwe.

concepts.name: Factors influencing mining and mining methods
concepts.description: Physical, economic and political factors that influence whether a mineral is mined (size, grade and depth of deposit, accessibility, transport, power, water, capital, markets and prices, technology, government policy); surface methods (open-cast/open-pit, strip, alluvial, dredging, quarrying) and underground methods (shaft, adit, drift) with their advantages and disadvantages.

concepts.name: Small-scale mining and gold panning
concepts.description: Prospecting methods including indigenous knowledge; physical and chemical properties used to identify alluvial minerals; gold panning methods; small-scale and artisanal mining in Zimbabwe: characteristics, contribution to the economy, problems (land degradation, mercury use, siltation, unsafe shafts, illegal mining) and solutions; the legal framework for mining rights in outline.

concepts.name: Processing minerals and beneficiation
concepts.description: How selected minerals are processed (for example gold ore crushing and extraction, platinum concentrating and smelting, chrome to ferrochrome, iron ore to steel, copper refining) in Zimbabwe and Africa; beneficiation and value addition: meaning, importance and challenges.

concepts.name: Mining, the environment and sustainable use
concepts.description: Environmental impacts of mining (land degradation, deforestation, water and air pollution, siltation, waste dumps) and their mitigation and rehabilitation; health and safety in mining; sustainable use of mineral resources (reuse, recycling, efficient extraction); cost-benefit analysis of a mining project. Out: the general EIA process (geo.environment.eia-land-use).

concepts.name: Environmental management, legislation and international agreements
concepts.description: Aspects of the environment (land, water, air), pristine and degraded environments, the meaning of environmental management and indigenous knowledge in it; Zimbabwe's environmental legislation and institutions (the Environmental Management Act and Agency, the Water Act and ZINWA, the Parks and Wild Life Act, the Forest Act) and their effectiveness and challenges; international treaties and protocols (UNFCCC, Kyoto, Montreal, Basel, Bamako, Ramsar, CITES, Zambezi basin agreements) and the pros and cons of domesticating them.

concepts.name: Land degradation: soil erosion, deforestation and desertification
concepts.description: Forms, causes and effects of land degradation: veld fires, soil erosion (sheet, rill, gully), siltation of rivers and dams, deforestation, uncontrolled sand abstraction, destruction of wetlands, desertification; mitigation and management (contour ridges, terracing, afforestation, conservation farming, controlled grazing, fireguards, gully reclamation) evaluated for sustainability.

concepts.name: Pollution and waste management
concepts.description: Water, air, land and noise pollution and graffiti: sources, effects on people and the environment, and control; solid-waste management (reduce, reuse, recycle; landfills; illegal dumping) in Zimbabwean towns; the social, economic and physical effects of environmental deterioration. Out: river pollution case study (geo.rivers.pollution).

concepts.name: Environmental impact assessment and land-use planning
concepts.description: Environmental management planning; the purpose and stages of an environmental impact assessment and its importance (including in mining); land-use zoning and land-use planning as a strategy for sustainable environmental management; planning laws (the Regional, Town and Country Planning Act; rural district councils); challenges and risk-informed land-use planning.

concepts.name: Farming systems and factors influencing agriculture
concepts.description: Farming as a system (physical, human and economic inputs; processes; outputs; feedback); types of farming (subsistence and commercial, arable, pastoral and mixed, intensive and extensive, hydroponics, aquaponics and aeroponics); physical, political and socio-economic factors influencing agriculture; elements of a communal farm.

concepts.name: Zimbabwe's natural (agro-ecological) regions
concepts.description: The natural farming regions I to V (with IIa and IIb): location, rainfall, temperature, soils and the farming activities suited to each; drawing and reading a map of the regions; how climate change is shifting them.

concepts.name: Farming types in Zimbabwe
concepts.description: Characteristics, benefits and challenges of subsistence and communal farming, and of commercial dairying, horticulture and market gardening, cattle ranching, mixed farming, plantation agriculture (tea, sugar cane, timber) and irrigation farming; named areas and schemes in Zimbabwe.

concepts.name: Land tenure and land reform in Zimbabwe
concepts.description: Land tenure systems (freehold, leasehold, communal, state land) and their advantages and disadvantages; land consolidation and fragmentation; aims, processes, outcomes and challenges of land reform and resettlement in Zimbabwe (the willing-buyer willing-seller phase and the accelerated fast-track phase; A1 and A2 resettlement models); stated neutrally and factually.

concepts.name: Farming challenges: climate change, pests and diseases
concepts.description: Effects of climate change on agriculture in Zimbabwe and southern Africa and mitigation and adaptation measures (conservation agriculture, drought-tolerant crops and breeds, irrigation, water harvesting, crop diversification); common crop and livestock pests and diseases (for example fall armyworm, locusts, quelea birds, tick-borne diseases, foot-and-mouth disease), their effects on productivity and manual, biological and chemical control.

concepts.name: Urban agriculture and agribusiness
concepts.description: Nature, advantages, disadvantages and problems of urban agriculture in Zimbabwean towns and solutions; agribusiness: types in Zimbabwe (input supply, processing, marketing, contract farming), sources of funding for small-scale agribusiness and its importance to individuals and the economy.

concepts.name: Global food supply and demand
concepts.description: Global patterns of calorie intake and reasons for them; reasons for changing global food production and consumption; the globalisation of food supplies (reasons and impacts on producers, consumers and the environment).

concepts.name: Food security and increasing food supply
concepts.description: Human and natural factors that reduce food supply; food insecurity and its problems in countries at different levels of development; strategies to increase food supply (irrigation, the Green Revolution, mechanisation, genetic modification, fertilisers, land reform, small-scale farming support) and an evaluation of food aid; the contribution of small-scale farmers to food security in Zimbabwe; a named country case study.

concepts.name: Types of industry and employment structure
concepts.description: Primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary industry with examples; the importance of each to Zimbabwe; employment structures of low-, middle- and high-income countries and how they change with development (the Clark-Fisher idea in outline).

concepts.name: Factors influencing the location of industry
concepts.description: Physical and human factors (raw materials, power, water, land, labour, capital, markets, transport, government policy, technology, communications, containerisation, agglomeration); raw-material-oriented, market-oriented and footloose industries; applying the factors to named industries in Zimbabwe.

concepts.name: Manufacturing and processing industries in Zimbabwe
concepts.description: Types and distribution of manufacturing and processing industries in Zimbabwe (the Harare, Bulawayo, Midlands and Mutare industrial areas; agro-processing such as sugar milling and textiles; metal and mineral processing); their importance; problems facing manufacturing (power, foreign currency, obsolete machinery, competition from imports, transport costs) and possible solutions.

concepts.name: Small and medium enterprises, the informal sector and occupational safety
concepts.description: Causes, characteristics and location of small to medium enterprises and informal industries in Zimbabwe (for example home industries and urban craft and metalwork clusters); their role in the economy; occupational safety and health measures in industry.

concepts.name: Globalisation
concepts.description: What globalisation means; its key features and causes (transport, communications, trade liberalisation); impacts on trade, transport, culture, communications and technology, positive and negative; a named country or area example.

concepts.name: Transnational corporations
concepts.description: What TNCs are, their global organisation (headquarters, research, production, sales) and why they locate where they do; advantages and disadvantages of TNCs for host countries; a named TNC case study.

concepts.name: The growth and management of tourism
concepts.description: Factors that have led to the growth of tourism; the Butler model of resort development and its strengths and limitations; economic, social and environmental benefits and problems of tourism at different scales; sustainable tourism and ecotourism strategies evaluated; a named country or area case study.

concepts.name: Service industries and tourism in Zimbabwe
concepts.description: Service (tertiary) and quaternary industries in Zimbabwe; tourism as a service industry: Zimbabwe's tourist attractions (Victoria Falls, Great Zimbabwe, Hwange, Mana Pools, Matobo, Lake Kariba, the Eastern Highlands), the importance of tourism, problems facing tourism and service industries and solutions.

concepts.name: Settlements: types, site, situation and patterns
concepts.description: Rural and urban settlements and their characteristics; site and situation and the factors that influence them (water, relief, defence, soils, transport); rural settlement patterns (nucleated, dispersed, linear) and their causes; siting settlements safely and disaster-resilient buildings and infrastructure.

concepts.name: Urbanisation and urban growth
concepts.description: Urbanisation and urban growth; reasons for differences in urban growth rates around the world; causes of rapid urban growth in low-income countries (rural-urban migration, push and pull factors, natural increase); the process of urbanisation in Zimbabwe.

concepts.name: Urban land use and urban models
concepts.description: Urban land-use zones (CBD, industrial, residential of different densities, recreational, rural-urban fringe) and their characteristics; the concentric zone, sector and multiple-nuclei models; applying the models to Zimbabwean towns such as Harare and Bulawayo.

concepts.name: Opportunities and challenges of urban growth
concepts.description: Opportunities of urban living (jobs, services, culture, housing); challenges of rapid urban growth (housing shortages, inequality, service provision, water and sanitation, waste, traffic congestion, unemployment, pollution); urban sprawl and its impact on the rural-urban fringe.

concepts.name: Managing urban growth
concepts.description: Strategies and techniques for managing urban growth (site-and-service schemes, upgrading, public transport, satellite towns, green belts, waste and water management, smart and sustainable cities) evaluated; a named urban area case study of causes, challenges and management.

concepts.name: Unplanned urban settlements
concepts.description: Characteristics of unplanned (informal) settlements; where they develop within and around towns; causes; social, economic and environmental effects; measures to improve them (upgrading, regularisation, low-cost housing).

concepts.name: Population terms and population data
concepts.description: Birth rate, death rate, natural increase, infant mortality rate, fertility rate, life expectancy, migration rate and how to calculate them; censuses and other sources; collecting, presenting and interpreting population data at local and national level.

concepts.name: Population structure and population pyramids
concepts.description: Constructing and interpreting population pyramids; factors influencing population structure (natural increase, net migration); youthful and ageing populations, their causes and impacts; dependency ratio; comparing Zimbabwe's pyramid with that of a high-income country.

concepts.name: Population distribution and density
concepts.description: Population distribution and density (calculation) in Zimbabwe, Africa and the world; physical and human factors causing dense and sparse populations; reading population distribution maps.

concepts.name: Population growth and the demographic transition model
concepts.description: Patterns and trends of global population growth; factors affecting growth and decline; effects of rapid growth and of decline; the demographic transition model, its stages, strengths and limitations and its application to Zimbabwe and other countries.

concepts.name: Population policies
concepts.description: Why countries have population policies; anti-natalist and pro-natalist policies with named examples; evaluating their effects on birth rates; a named country case study.

concepts.name: Migration: types, causes and impacts
concepts.description: Types and categories of migration (internal: rural-urban, urban-rural, urban-urban, rural-rural; international; voluntary and forced; economic migrants, asylum seekers and refugees); push and pull factors; impacts on migrants and on sending and receiving areas; managing international migration; a named international migration case study.

concepts.name: Population and disease
concepts.description: Common diseases in developing countries (water-borne, vector-borne and nutritional diseases, HIV and AIDS) and in developed countries (lifestyle diseases); reasons for the differences; social and economic effects of disease on populations.

concepts.name: Modes of transport
concepts.description: Road, rail, air, water and pipeline transport: characteristics, advantages and disadvantages and how modes have changed; choosing a mode for a given cargo or journey.

concepts.name: Transport networks and network analysis
concepts.description: Zimbabwe's road, rail and air network, its links to ports and neighbouring countries (for example the Beira, Beitbridge and Victoria Falls routes), the network in the region and Africa; network analysis (nodes, links, connectivity, beta index, detour index); flow-line diagrams; transport problems and solutions.

concepts.name: Trade: patterns, imbalances and trading blocs
concepts.description: Why trade happens; domestic and foreign trade; imports, exports and the balance of trade; trade patterns of Zimbabwe, SADC, Africa and the world; trade imbalances within countries, between regions and internationally; trading blocs (SADC, COMESA, ECOWAS, EU, OPEC as a producers' organisation) and why they form.

concepts.name: Measuring development
concepts.description: Economic and social indicators of development (GDP, GNP, GNI per capita, literacy rate, life expectancy, infant mortality, calorie intake, doctors per person, the Human Development Index); using indicators to compare countries and their limitations; quality of life and standard of living.

concepts.name: Uneven development and the development gap
concepts.description: Social, economic, environmental and historical reasons for differences in development; the development gap; the current global pattern of low-, middle- and high-income countries.

concepts.name: Sustainable development and reducing uneven development
concepts.description: Definitions of sustainable development; social, economic and environmental strategies to achieve it; evaluating trade (including fair trade), international aid (types, benefits and problems) and debt relief as ways of reducing uneven development; a named LIC or MIC case study.
